views.name: fda_food_enforcement_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  recall_number,
  event_id,
  center_classification_date,
  report_date,
  termination_date,
  recall_initiation_date,
  SAFE_CAST(postal_code AS STRING) AS postal_code,
  UPPER(TRIM(state)) AS state_abbr,
  TRIM(city) AS city,
  TRIM(recalling_firm) AS recalling_firm,
  TRIM(product_type) AS product_type,
  TRIM(product_description) AS product_description,
  TRIM(distribution_pattern) AS distribution_pattern,
  TRIM(reason_for_recall) AS reason_for_recall,
  TRIM(status) AS status,
  UPPER(TRIM(classification)) AS classification,
  TRIM(product_quantity) AS product_quantity,
  IFNULL(NULLIF(TRIM(distribution_pattern), ''), NULL) IS NOT NULL AS has_distribution_pattern,
  IFNULL(NULLIF(TRIM(product_quantity), ''), NULL) IS NOT NULL AS has_quantity,
  COALESCE(country, '') AS country,
  address_1,
  address_2,
  more_code_info
FROM `bigquery-public-data.fda_food.food_enforcement`
grain: recall_number, event_id — one row per enforcement/recall event record
views.description: Normalized, cleaned projection of FDA food enforcement (recall) records. Use this as a canonical enforcement-event relation for counts, joins to geography, time-series, and text analysis. Preserves recall identifiers and key descriptive fields, converts date strings to DATE (already DATE in schema), canonicalizes status/classification casing, and exposes simple derived flags (has_distribution_pattern, has_quantity). | Use for: counts of recalls by state, country, classification, or status; time-series of recall activity (by report_date/recall_initiation_date); text searches on product_description or reason_for_recall; joins to geographic tables via state_abbr or postal_code

views.name: fdic_branch_locations_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  fdic_certificate_number,
  institution_name,
  branch_name,
  branch_number,
  main_office,
  TRIM(branch_address) AS branch_address,
  TRIM(branch_city) AS branch_city,
  SUBSTR(TRIM(zip_code), 1, 5) AS zip5,
  TRIM(branch_county) AS branch_county,
  NULLIF(TRIM(county_fips_code), '') AS county_fips_code,
  UPPER(TRIM(state)) AS state_abbr,
  TRIM(state_name) AS state_name,
  TRIM(institution_class) AS institution_class,
  TRIM(cbsa_fips_code) AS cbsa_fips_code,
  TRIM(cbsa_name) AS cbsa_name,
  cbsa_division_flag,
  cbsa_division_fips_code,
  cbsa_division_name,
  cbsa_metro_flag,
  cbsa_metro_fips_code,
  cbsa_metro_name,
  cbsa_micro_flag,
  csa_flag,
  csa_fips_code,
  csa_name,
  fdic_uninum,
  service_type,
  date_established,
  last_updated
FROM `bigquery-public-data.fdic_banks.locations`
grain: fdic_uninum or (fdic_certificate_number, branch_number) — one row per branch location
views.description: Cleaned projection of FDIC branch location rows. Use for spatial aggregations, institution-level rollups, CBSA/CSA analysis, and linking to FIPS/state tables. Preserves FDIC identifiers, institution name, address fields, geography codes, class flags, and exposes a main_office boolean and normalized ZIP and county FIPS. | Use for: branch counts per state/city/CBSA; identify main office vs branch locations; time-based queries on date_established or last_updated; join branches to state/FIPS crosswalks or to enforcement records by state
